chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ali ibn Ziyad, who said: 'Ali ibn Baseer wrote to him, asking him to write for him at the bottom of his letter a supplication that he would teach him, so that by it he would be protected from sins, comprehensive for the world and the Hereafter.

So he (peace be upon him) wrote in his own handwriting: 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. O He Who Manifested the beautiful and concealed the ugly, and did not tear the veil from me. O Generous of Pardon, O Excellent in Overlooking, O Vast in Forgiveness, O Extender of the Two Hands with Mercy, O Companion of every secret conversation, and O End-point of every complaint. O Generous of Pardoning, O Magnificent in Bestowing Favors, O Initiator of every blessing before it is deserved. O My Lord, O My Master, O My Lord, O My Helper. Send blessings upon Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad. And I ask You that You do not make me in the Fire, then ask whatever seems good to You.'

key_terms.صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: Send blessings upon Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad
key_terms.يَا بَاسِطَ الْيَدَيْنِ بِالرَّحْمَةِ: O Extender of the Two Hands with Mercy

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for protection from sins and comprehensive needs in the world and Hereafter?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication was personally written by Imam Ali (peace be upon him) in response to a request from his companion Ali ibn Baseer, highlighting the intimate transmission of spiritual remedies within the Shia scholarly chain. It uniquely combines divine attributes of modesty and generosity with a profound eschatological hope, asking that God’s pleasure in granting mercy not be contingent upon the supplicant’s prior merit, thereby emphasizing grace over strict retribution.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, and a number of our companions, from Sahl BiN Ziyad, altogether from Ali Bin Ziyad who said, 
‘Ali Bin Baseer wrote to him<sup>asws</sup>, asking him<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> write to him at the bottom of his<sup>asws</sup> letter, teaching him a supplication he can supplicate with, so he can be saved from the comprehensive sins of the world and the Hereafter.

So heasws wrote in hisasws own handwriting: ‘In the Name of Allahazwj the Beneficent, the Merciful. O the Oneazwj Who Manifest the beauty and Veils the ugliness, and does not Tear down the Veil from me. O Benevolent, the Pardon, O Excellent Overlooker! O Extensive of Forgiveness! O Most Extensive of the Hands with the Mercy! O Companion of every conversation, and O the End-point of every complaint! O the Benevolent Excuser! O the Magnifier of the Favours! O the Initiator of every Bounty it is being deserved! O Lordazwj! O Chief! O Master! O Rescuer! Send Salawāt upon Muhammadsaww and the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww; and I ask Youazwj that Youazwj do not Make me to be in the Fire’. Then ask whatever comes to you’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa and A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad all from Ali ibn Ziyad has said that Ali ibn Basir once wrote to the Imam asking him to write for him a supplication at the bottom of the page of his own letter with instructions, a supplication that would keep him safe from sins and with comprehensive benefits in this world and in the hereafter.

The Imam (a.s.) wrote to me in his own handwriting: “(I begin) in the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful, O the One who manifests the good things, hides the bad ones, does not rip apart the covering from me (my privacy), O magnanimous in pardoning, O the One who overlooks faults with grace, whose forgiveness is vast, whose hands are wide open with kindness, who is the companion of every whisperer, the end receiver of complaints, who honorably pardons, the great provider of favors, the initiator of bounties before a recipient would deserve it, O Lord, O Master, O Guardian, O Rescuer, grant al-Salat (favors) upon Muhammad and his family, and I plead before You not to place me in the fire.’”
